title: Chicxulub impact tsunami and Gulf of Mexico megaflood deposits
summary: The Chicxulub asteroid impact about 66 million years ago set off a tsunami. Drilled rock from the crater peak ring records floodwaters carrying land debris into the crater within days, with waves several hundred metres high, and seismic images under Louisiana show giant ripples interpreted as the tsunami marking the Gulf floor.

uncertainty.note: Both sources say "66 million years ago" / "66 million year old"; the bracket is a rounding allowance. The atlas Chicxulub record places the K-Pg boundary at 66.043 Ma.

as_recorded.value: 66 million years ago; the wave flooded the crater within days
66 million year old Chicxulub Impact tsunami; seismic reflections from about 1500 m underground

where.modern_name: Chicxulub crater, Yucatan Peninsula, Mexico (centre; deposits extend across the Gulf of Mexico)
where.historical_name: Impact site on the Yucatan carbonate platform, Gulf of Mexico (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point 21.40, -89.52 reconstructed to 66 Ma. PALEOMAP gives 25.49 N, 71.07 W. The spread in absolute position between models reflects differing reference frames.

importance.justification: Physical evidence of the immediate ocean-scale effects of the impact that ended the Cretaceous.

related.because: The tsunami was a direct consequence of the impact.
